summary: The bill requires operating system providers to collect every user's date of birth during setup or use, obtain parental verification for anyone under 18, share the data with app developers for their own checks, and give parents control over what minors can access, with FTC enforcement.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates new regulatory requirements enforced by the FTC but does not authorize or appropriate any new federal spending, programs, or funding mechanisms. It is purely a mandate on private companies with enforcement via existing FTC authority.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection.
No provisions address healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
No provisions relate to firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.
No provisions address immigration, visas, border security, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions address reproductive rights, abortion access, or restrictions.
No provisions address military funding, defense programs, or national security spending.
No provisions address environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy standards.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net expansions or reductions.
While the bill involves parental controls over device access, it does not address school funding, curriculum, federal education policy, or school choice programs.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization policies.
No provisions address deficit spending, debt reduction targets, or fiscal policy.
No provisions address legal protections or restrictions related to LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign assistance, international aid, or diplomatic funding.
No provisions address voting access, voter ID, or election administration.

The bill mandates that operating system providers collect date-of-birth data for age verification, share limited data with app developers, implement data protection standards against breaches, and allow parental controls. It also empowers the FTC to enforce these requirements as unfair or deceptive practices. This constitutes new regulatory oversight on technology companies regarding data handling and user verification, directly engaging the topic of tech regulation and privacy.
No provisions address worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights protections, or anti-discrimination rules.
